subject: Computer Networking
title: DDoS Attacks
description: A micro-lesson that makes DDoS Attacks usable.

hook.text: Millions of fake requests hit a server at once. Real users can't get through. The service is down.

buildup.text: DDoS — Distributed Denial of Service — uses botnets of compromised devices to flood a target with traffic.

discovery.text: Attackers exploit IoT devices, misconfigured servers, and amplification techniques to multiply their bandwidth.

twist.text: You can rent a DDoS attack for as little as $20 online. The barrier to entry is shockingly low.

climax.text: Cloudflare and AWS Shield absorb DDoS traffic at the edge. Mitigation is now a standard cloud service.

punchline.text: DDoS doesn't hack in. It drowns the front door.

quiz.question: What is the goal of a DDoS attack?
options: To overwhelm a service so legitimate users can't access it
To steal data from a database
To install malware on a server

details.summary: DDoS attacks flood a target with overwhelming traffic from thousands of compromised devices, exhausting bandwidth, server resources, or application capacity.
details.whyItMatters: DDoS attacks can take any online service offline regardless of how well the application is built. Understanding attack types enables choosing appropriate mitigation strategies.
takeaways: DDoS uses distributed sources to overwhelm a target with traffic
Volumetric, protocol, and application-layer attacks target different resources
Cloud-based scrubbing services absorb attack traffic at scale

faq.question: How large can DDoS attacks get?
faq.answer: Record attacks have exceeded 3 terabits per second using amplification techniques. Botnets of millions of compromised IoT devices generate massive traffic. Even smaller attacks of a few gigabits per second can overwhelm most organizations without DDoS protection services.

faq.question: How do you defend against DDoS attacks?
faq.answer: Cloud-based DDoS mitigation services like Cloudflare, AWS Shield, and Akamai absorb attack traffic across their global networks. Rate limiting, geographic filtering, and challenge-based verification filter malicious requests. Over-provisioning bandwidth and using CDNs help absorb smaller attacks.
